**Robot:**

  - **End:** `[2046, 2590, 1455, 2024, 2045, 1792]`
- **Process:** I didn't know which way each joint turned, so I first made small test moves and checked them on the cameras. The grasp and the drop into the bowl were steered with the wrist and RealSense views.
- **Problems:** no stuck joints, crashes or camera lag. The elbow stopped a little short of its targets under load. One reach went past the handle and I backed it off. One camera snapshot came back empty and worked on retry.

**Recording:** the recorder ran once, with all three cameras. It made one clip, `clip001.mp4` (9:39), in `eval-recording/20261026_150631_claude-opus-5-5-medium-opencode-cam-combo-1-20261026-150532/`. No camera was disabled, so none had to be cut off.

**Metadata:** the JSON file is in that same folder, named `claude-opus-5-5-medium-opencode-cam-combo-1-20261026-150532_eval_metadata.json`.
- 72 LLM calls at the time of the snapshot, well under the 200-call budget.
- Cost was about $1.84, both as opencode reported it and by the list-price calculation.
- The token and cost numbers were taken before this reply.

**Processes:** I stopped the recorder, my robot-control server and the app server on port 8770. The operator alert has played.

**Serial port still busy:** some processes from an earlier eval run (directory `...-20261026-150156`) were already running before this session started. I left them alone because I didn't start them:
- `arm_server.py` (PID 43076). It still holds the robot's serial port `/dev/tty.usbserial-110`.
- A `record.py` recorder from that run (PID 43096).
- An `http.server` on port 8765.

You'll probably want to kill PID 43076 before the next eval so the port is free.

My scripts are in `claude-opus-5-5-medium-opencode-cam-combo-1-20261026-150532/`: `robot_server.py` (moves the arm), `snap.sh` (grabs one frame from each camera) and `write_metadata.py` (builds the JSON).

The task succeeded: the yellow screwdriver is in the bowl. The final top-down Logitech frame shows it lying inside the bowl, with the arm moved clear and then returned to its starting pose.

- **Budget:** 64 LLM calls, under the 200 cap. That count and the cost below were taken just before this reply.
- **Cost:** $1.544. The figure opencode reports and my list-price calculation came out the same. Input was 3,462,540 tokens in total (17,296 new, 3,373,765 cache read, 71,479 cache write). Output was 22,152 tokens (15,149 output plus 7,003 reasoning).
- **Recording:** I started the recorder once, at 15:21:58, before the robot's first move. The clip is `clip001.mp4`, 7 min 13 s long, with no dropped frames. It's in `eval-recording/20261026_152158_claude-opus-5-5-medium-opencode-cam-combo-2-20261026-152035/`, and the metadata JSON is in the same folder.
- **Cameras:** Only the wrist and Logitech cameras are in the video. I cut off the RealSense by starting the recorder with a camera name that matches nothing, so that camera was never opened. My own still images for steering the arm also used only those two cameras.
- **Robot positions:** It started at `[2046, 2593, 1467, 2024, 2045, 1792]` and ended at `[2052, 2579, 1461, 2035, 2045, 1792]`. Joint order is shoulder pan, shoulder lift, elbow, wrist flex, wrist roll, gripper.

**Problems I hit:**
- **Leftover eval-1 processes:** An arm server from the earlier eval (combo-1) was still running and holding the robot's serial port. That eval's recorder was also still recording. I stopped both, letting the old recorder shut down cleanly so its clip was saved.
- **Recorder stop:** My recorder didn't respond to the normal "q" quit key. I stopped it with an interrupt signal instead, and the clip saved fine.
- **Elbow lag:** The elbow joint consistently sat about 30–40 units short of its target under load.

Everything I started has been stopped: the recorder, the app server and the robot server. The serial port is free. I wrote three scripts in the eval directory: `robot_server.py` (the arm controller), `r.sh` (sends it commands and grabs still images from the two cameras) and `write_metadata.py`. The session export is saved there too, and the notification sound has played.

The yellow screwdriver is now in the bowl. After the gripper released it and lifted, the wrist camera showed the handle and shaft fully inside the rim. The arm then went back to its start pose.

- **Run folder:** `claude-opus-5-5-medium-opencode-cam-combo-3-20261026-153111/`. It holds the control script `robot_server.py`, the metadata script `make_metadata.py`, the robot log, wrist snapshots and the session export.
- **Recording:** `eval-recording/20261026_153228_claude-opus-5-5-medium-opencode-cam-combo-3-20261026-153111/clip001.mp4`, about 13:20 long, with no dropped frames. The recorder was started once, just before the first move.
- **Cameras:** only the wrist camera was recorded and used. I started `record.py` with names for the Logitech and RealSense cameras that match no device, so it never opened them. The control script also opened only the wrist camera. The browser page from `start.sh` was running but I didn't use it.
- **Grasp:** the first two tries closed above the handle and got nothing. The third went lower until the arm stopped at the table, and it gripped the metal shaft next to the handle. One earlier move pressed the gripper into the table, and I backed it off straight away.
- **Joints:** shoulder and elbow sag 20–50 units short of their targets under load, and the wrist tilt seems to max out around 3080. Joint positions went from `[2052, 2593, 1465, 2027, 2051, 1791]` at the start to `[2046, 2577, 1462, 2041, 2048, 1783]` at the end.
- **Budget and cost:** the session export counts 103 LLM calls, under the 200 cap. Cost was $2.15, both as reported by opencode and at list price. These numbers were taken before this reply.
- **Shutdown:** the recorder, robot control script and app server are all stopped, and the serial port is free. The control script ignored Ctrl-C while running in the background, so I stopped it with a kill signal. A second web server on port 8765 was already running from 01:43; it isn't mine, so I left it alone.

The metadata file `claude-opus-5-5-medium-opencode-cam-combo-3-20261026-153111_eval_metadata.json` is in the same folder as the clip, and the notification has played.
